blocks.text: Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) reports that Hadhrat Sa'd bin Ubaadah (RA) once asked, "If I found a man with my wife, am I not allowed to touch him until I present four witnesses?" "That's right," Rasulullaah ﷺ replied. Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) then said, "That cannot be! I swear by the Being Who has sent you with the truth that before that I would speed up his journey with my sword." "Listen to what your leader has to say," Rasulullaah ﷺ said to the Sahabah (RA), "He is extremely possessive, but I am more possessive than him and Allaah is more possessive than I."[^1]

A lengthy narration from Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) adds that the Sahabah (RA) said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Do not rebuke him because he is an extremely possessive person. By Allaah! He has only married virgins and because of his possessiveness, none of us has ever dared to marry any woman he has divorced." Hadhrat Sa'd (RA) then said, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! I know that the injunction (of presenting four witnesses to prove adultery) is true and is from Allaah but I find it strange that when I find a man rubbing his thighs against those of an immoral woman, I am unable to move him until I bring four witnesses. By Allaah! By the time I come with them, he would have fulfilled his desire (and left)."[^2]

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) reports that when Rasulullaah ﷺ left her one night, she became extremely jealous. Rasulullaah ﷺ then returned to see what she was doing and commented, "What is the matter, O Aa'isha? Have you been overcome with possessiveness?" Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) replied, "Why should someone like myself not be possessive over someone like yourself?" "Your Shaytaan must have come to you," Rasulullaah ﷺ remarked. "O Rasulullaah ﷺ!" Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) asked, "Is there a Shaytaan with me?" "Certainly," Rasulullaah ﷺ replied. "And with you, O Rasulullaah ﷺ?" Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) enquired. "Yes," Rasulullaah ﷺ replied, "but Allaah has assisted me and he has become a Muslim (and therefore does not influence me to do evil)."[^3]

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) narrates, "When Rasulullaah ﷺ married Ummu Salamah (RA), I became extremely depressed because people always told us about her beauty. When I managed to secretly steal a glance at her, I found her to be much more beautiful than people had described. I then mentioned this to Hafsah (RA) (Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) and Hadhrat Hafsah (RA) were extremely close). She said, 'By Allaah! This is only because of your extreme possessiveness. She cannot be as beautiful as you people say.' When Hafsah (RA) also managed to steal a glance at her, she said, 'I have seen her and I swear by Allaah that she is not as beautiful as you say. In fact, she is not even close to what you have described, although I do admit that she is pretty.'"
Muslim, as quoted in Mishkaatul Masaabeeh (Pg.278).
Abu Ya'la and Ahmad. Haythami (Vol.5 Pg.12) has commented on the chain of narrators.
Muslim, as quoted in Mishkaatul Masaabeeh (Pg.280).
